title: How countries, cities, and attractions market to Chinese tourists across WeChat, Douyin, RED, and more. — Shanghai Jungle

facts.fact: Chinese travelers made 145 million outbound trips in 2024, spending 5.75 trillion RMB, a 17% year-on-year increase.
facts.quote: Chinese travelers made 145 million outbound trips in 2024, spending 5.75 trillion RMB — a 17% year-on-year increase.

facts.fact: The page projects Chinese outbound trips will reach 170 million by 2026.
facts.quote: By 2026, that number is expected to reach 170 million trips.

facts.fact: The page projects Chinese outbound tourism spending will exceed $386 billion by 2033, growing at a 13.5% CAGR.
facts.quote: By 2033, Chinese outbound tourism spending is projected to exceed $386 billion

facts.fact: The page cites a projected 13.5% CAGR for Chinese outbound tourism spending.
facts.quote: Growing at 13.5% CAGR, making China the world's largest outbound tourism source market.

facts.fact: The page says 75% of Chinese respondents were planning outbound travel, the highest share recorded since post-pandemic surveying began in late 2022.
facts.quote: The highest percentage recorded since post-pandemic surveying began in late 2022.

facts.fact: The page states Q4 outbound bookings surpassed 2019 levels by over 20%.
facts.quote: Recovered to near pre-pandemic levels, with Q4 bookings surpassing 2019 by over 20%.

facts.fact: The page says visa-free agreements with 45+ countries are a driver of the projected 2026 Chinese travel growth.
facts.quote: Driven by expanded visa-free agreements with 45+ countries

facts.fact: Southeast Asia accounts for 37% of Chinese outbound overnight visitors, Northeast Asia 29%, and Europe 21%.
facts.quote: Southeast Asia leads with 37% of outbound overnight visitors, followed by Northeast Asia at 29% and Europe at 21%.

facts.fact: The page states Chinese arrivals to Europe and the Americas remain 40–50% below 2019 levels.
facts.quote: Chinese arrivals to longer-haul destinations like Europe and the Americas are still 40–50% below 2019 levels

facts.fact: The page says China's visa-waiver list covers 45 countries and includes Italy, Germany, Saudi Arabia, Australia, France, Argentina, and Brazil.
facts.quote: China's 45-country visa-waiver list now includes Italy, Germany, Saudi Arabia, Australia, France, Argentina, and Brazil

facts.fact: The UAE extended its visa-free policy for Chinese tourists to 90 days in 2025.
facts.quote: The UAE extended its visa-free policy for Chinese tourists to 90 days in 2025.

facts.fact: Micro-KOL travel promotion posts cost around 2,000 RMB per post, according to the page.
facts.quote: Pricing ranges from around 2,000 RMB per post for micro-KOLs to 300,000+ RMB for celebrity-level partnerships.

facts.fact: The page defines Millennials and Gen Z as those born 1985–2005 and describes them as the largest traveler segment.
facts.quote: Millennials and Gen Z (born 1985–2005) are the largest segment.

facts.fact: The page identifies the silver generation as travelers aged 60 and over.
facts.quote: Silver generation (60+)

facts.fact: The page states Google, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and Twitter are blocked in China.
facts.quote: Google is blocked. Facebook is blocked. Instagram is blocked. YouTube is blocked. Twitter is blocked.

facts.fact: Shanghai Jungle's recommended first-90-days playbook includes publishing 10–15 posts on a Xiaohongshu Enterprise or Pro profile in weeks 2–4.
facts.quote: Publish your first 10–15 posts: stunning destination photos with detailed Chinese captions covering practical travel info, seasonal highlights, and local culture.

facts.fact: Shanghai Jungle recommends identifying 3–5 mid-tier travel KOLs for a first KOL campaign in weeks 8–12 of the 90-day playbook.
facts.quote: Identify 3–5 mid-tier travel KOLs whose audience matches your target traveler profile.

facts.fact: According to Shanghai Jungle, building a meaningful Chinese digital presence takes 6–12 months.
facts.quote: Building a meaningful Chinese digital presence takes 6–12 months.

facts.fact: Shanghai Jungle's FAQ says destinations should expect to invest 3–6 months before seeing meaningful traction from China marketing.
facts.quote: Expect to invest 3–6 months before seeing meaningful traction.

facts.fact: Shanghai Jungle's FAQ states that a well-executed China marketing strategy typically shows clear ROI by month 12.
facts.quote: By month 12, a well-executed strategy typically shows clear ROI through measurable increases in Chinese visitor numbers and spending.

facts.fact: In Shanghai Jungle's 90-day playbook, the WeChat Official Account setup (Service Account registration and menu design) is scheduled for weeks 1–3.
facts.quote: Set Up Your WeChat Official Account (Weeks 1–3)

facts.fact: In Shanghai Jungle's 90-day playbook, the Mafengwo and Ctrip optimization step is scheduled for weeks 4–8.
facts.quote: Optimize Your Mafengwo and Ctrip Presence (Weeks 4–8)

facts.fact: In Shanghai Jungle's 90-day playbook, the first KOL campaign launch is scheduled for weeks 8–12.
facts.quote: Launch Your First KOL Campaign (Weeks 8–12)
